headline: Greenland Hits Pause on Seabed Mining Until 2029
meta_description: Greenland's parliament unanimously votes to suspend seabed mining licensing, protecting the fishing industry that underpins 90% of exports.
summary_short: All 17 present members of Greenland's parliament voted to pause seabed mining until 2029, protecting marine ecosystems vital to the nation's economy.
body:
Greenland's parliament has taken an unprecedented step toward environmental caution, voting unanimously to suspend seabed mining licenses until at least 2029. On October 15, all 17 members present—across all political parties—supported a proposal that asks the government to draft legislation by early 2027 formalizing the pause. The decision comes as a deliberate choice to buy time for careful consideration rather than permanent protection. "This is a decision to decide. An important one, and not the same thing as protection," said Jenseeraq Poulsen, executive director of Oceans North Kalaallit Nunaat, an environmental nonprofit. The timing is striking: the vote happened just one day after U.S. President Donald Trump announced plans for "massive" mineral exploration in Greenland—a statement that underscores the international pressure the island nation faces.

The resolution, originally proposed in February 2026 by Pipaluk Lynge of the Inuit Ataqatigiit party, centers on a simple economic reality: Greenland's fishing industry generates more than 90% of the nation's exports. Deep-sea mining poses direct risks to fish populations, game animals, and the marine environment itself. "Economically, Greenland lives from the sea," Poulsen emphasized. "Any activity that puts the productivity of our waters at risk is not a diversification of the economy, it is a wager against the part of it that already works."

The suspension is not permanent. According to parliament member Juno Berthelsen, the halt expires December 31, 2029, but can be extended by two additional years. This structure allows Greenland to reassess deep-sea mining's viability without foreclosing future options entirely—a pragmatic balance between protecting what sustains the nation today and remaining open to tomorrow's opportunities.
quick_facts: All 17 present parliament members voted unanimously across party lines
Fishing industry accounts for over 90% of Greenland's exports
Mining suspension set to expire December 31, 2029, with potential two-year extension
Original proposal introduced February 2026 by Pipaluk Lynge
Vote took place October 15, one day after Trump's mineral exploration statement
